speaking_points: Set up the question: how can a large catalog be explored through content similarity?
Explain catalog discovery and segmentation; clarify this is not a recommendation engine.
State the clustering question and why labels are unavailable.
Report 7,787 records, 12 observed columns, and date-added range 2008–2021; flag the 2019-brief vs 2021-file mismatch.
Explain preserved missing metadata, zero exact duplicates, whitespace normalization, and retained unusual titles.
Show type mix (5,377 Movies; 2,410 TV Shows), add-year and release-year trends, ratings, country/type heatmap, genres, and duration.
Explain chi-square and Mann–Whitney results. Highlight non-monotonic TV shares across eras: {'2008-2014': 0.21052631578947367, '2015-2017': 0.32801822323462415, '2018-2021': 0.3038229376257545}.
Describe combined fields, conservative text cleaning, TF-IDF vs counts, sparse vectors, and 100-component SVD.
Show elbow and silhouette evidence; explain the 1% tie rule and selected K=9.
Explain Ward/average linkage sample comparison, selected ward with 10 groups, and sampled dendrogram.
Compare silhouette (0.177 vs 0.126) and show cluster sizes, terms, and representative titles.
Present clusters as catalog organization hypotheses and possible future recommender preprocessing; ask stakeholders to validate.
Mention provenance mismatch, missing fields, internal metrics, metadata-driven similarity, and sampled hierarchy.
Restate what was learned, what clusters can support, and what evidence is needed before operational use.
